promises.promise: Bring federal dollars home to CA-45 communities.
promises.why: Money was secured and delivered. The figures come from his office and were not independently audited.

actions.text: House appropriators advanced more than $14 million for 15 of his community projects (Jul 2025).
Delivered $3.15 million for the Del Amo Boulevard bridge in Cerritos.
Secured $1 million for Garden Grove firefighters.
Delivered $1 million to Cypress for flood prevention.
Presented $850,000 to the Buena Park Library District.
Delivered $925,000 for public safety in Artesia.
GKN Aerospace chemical leak in Garden Grove: demanded answers from GKN with Rep. Robert Garcia (May 2026).
Introduced H.R. 10108, the Hazardous Materials Transparency Act (Aug 2026).
Issued a statement on GKN's $125 million settlement (Oct 2026).

promises.promise: small businesses are the backbone of our economy
promises.why: His own bill cleared the House. It still needs Senate action.

actions.text: His bill H.R. 5788 (504 Program Risk Oversight Act) passed the House on Jan 20, 2026, and was sent to the Senate.
Cosponsored H.R. 787 (Plain Language in Contracting Act), which passed the House in June 2025.
Ranking Member of the Small Business oversight subcommittee.

promises.promise: Protect veterans' jobs and benefits and keep a strong national defense.
promises.why: The defense and benefits wins are real, but his veteran-jobs bill is stalled.

actions.text: Cosponsored the Major Richard Star Act (H.R. 2102), which passed the House 392–18 on Nov 12, 2026.
Voted yes on the final FY26 NDAA (Dec 10, 2025), citing the 3.8% troop pay raise. He had voted no on the House version in September.
His first bill, H.R. 1637 (Protect Veteran Jobs Act), has had no action since it was introduced on Feb 26, 2025.

promises.promise: Oppose cuts to Social Security and Medicare.
promises.why: His votes have been defensive and consistent. No bill he leads has become law.

actions.text: Voted no on H.R. 1 (May 22 and Jul 3, 2025).
Voted for H.R. 5348 (Social Security Child Protection Act), which passed 386–0 on Dec 1, 2025.
Introduced H.R. 6678 (Senior Legal Hotline Act). Held town halls in Cerritos, Buena Park and Westminster.

promises.promise: Stand firm against Chinese Communist rule and push for human rights in Vietnam.
promises.why: There is steady activity, but none of the resolutions has been adopted yet.

actions.text: Introduced Black April resolutions (2025 and 2026), a Vietnamese Heritage Flag resolution and H.R. 7969 (Combating CCP Influence Act).
Got an appropriations amendment passed to fund the U.S.–Vietnam Human Rights Dialogue (Jul 2026).
Wrote letters about prisoners of conscience, including journalist Le Huu Minh Tuan, and announced a State Department response in Oct 2026.

promises.promise: Lower costs for families, with tax cuts for middle-class families and small businesses.
promises.why: His central campaign issue, but none of these bills has had committee action.

actions.text: Co-founded the Lowering Costs Caucus with Reps. Landsman and Scholten (Jun 2025).
Introduced H.R. 4746 (Baby Food Tax Relief Act). Cosponsored the Toll of Tariffs Act, Stop Price Gouging in Grocery Stores Act and Stop the Trump Electricity Price Hikes Act.

promises.promise: healthcare should be a right, not a privilege
promises.why: His votes match the promise, but the cuts became law and the credit extension hasn't been enacted.

actions.text: Voted no on both House votes on the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (Medicaid and ACA cuts), which passed anyway.
Cosponsored H.R. 4849 to make enhanced ACA credits permanent. He voted Yea when a 3-year extension (H.R. 1834) passed the House 230–196 on Jan 8, 2026.
Voted no on funding bills that let ACA credits lapse.

promises.promise: ensure that all workers can afford housing
promises.why: None of the housing bills he leads or cosponsors has advanced.

actions.text: Introduced H.R. 10613 (Housing COST Act, Sep 2026). Cosponsored the Affordable Housing Credit Improvement Act.
Delivered $250K for affordable housing in Orange. Urged the President to sign the ROAD to Housing Act.

promises.promise: Oppose mass deportations, support reform with a path to citizenship, and hold ICE accountable.
promises.why: His accountability bills haven't moved, and his Laken Riley yes vote complicates his record on this promise.

actions.text: Introduced H.R. 9883 (Private Detention Corporate Accountability Act). Cosponsored ICE and CBP accountability bills. All remain in committee.
Voted no on DHS funding without ICE reforms (Jan–Mar 2026), per his office.
Voted for the Laken Riley Act (Jan 22, 2025), breaking with most Democrats.

promises.promise: Derek will fight to end this culture of corruption in our politics.
promises.why: The House passed a stock-trading bill with his vote, but it was the Republican version most Democrats opposed. The bans he cosponsored have not advanced.

actions.text: Cosponsored stock-trading bans H.R. 7852 (No Getting Rich in Congress Act) and STOCK Act 2.0.
Voted for the Epstein Files Transparency Act (passed 427–1, Nov 18, 2025).
Voted for the Republican-led Stop Insider Trading Act (H.R. 7008), which passed 232–198 on Jul 22, 2026. Democrats opposed it 13–198.

promises.promise: Codify a national right to abortion care.
promises.why: He is on record in support, but all three bills are in committee and have little chance in this House.

actions.text: Cosponsored H.R. 12 (Women's Health Protection Act), the Right to IVF Act and the Stop Comstock Act.
